topic.title: Costco's membership fees bring in billions, most of its whole profit, while the cart barely earns

title: Costco's profit was $9.23B. The card paid 64% of it
description:
How can a card you show at the door be worth $5.91B to Costco?
Data: Costco Wholesale · Sep 2026. Net sales $297.25B, net income $9.23B, membership fees $5.91B in fiscal 2026.
An animated story told with official figures; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Would you renew your card? Comment

lines.text: Costco's whole profit last year was $9.23B.
And a plastic card covered 64% of it.
Not the groceries. So where does all the cart money go?
Rohan's cart is one tiny piece of the $297.25B Costco sold that year.
Yet the whole profit is just 3.1% of those sales. Nearly every dollar pays for the goods.
The real money waits at the door. Every member pays for the card, every single year.
Those cards brought in $5.91B in one year.
That's 64% of the profit, from a card. The cart is the bait. Would you renew yours?
